name: Gas cylinders (propane, CO2, air)
summary: Pressure cylinders for propane, butane, CO2, air and welding gases. Keep them upright, outdoors and away from heat, and never cut or drill one, even when empty: a used propane cylinder still holds some gas, and a tank under pressure may explode if it is altered (CT DEEP propane).
uses: Propane for cooking, heating and lights
CO2 and air for tyres and air tools
Running a generator converted to propane
identify: Propane bottles on grills, patio heaters, campers and forklifts (horizontal tanks), and in exchange cages outside shops; CO2 at bars, restaurants and paintball shops; air tanks at dive shops and fire stations. The collar is stamped with the gas, the test date and the empty weight, marked TW for tare weight. Don't try to take the valve out of a propane cylinder: that needs special equipment and training (CT DEEP propane). An air-compressor tank is a different case: see the guide Hot work on drums, tanks and cylinders. Forklift tanks usually feed liquid propane, not gas: never connect one to a grill, heater, stove or lamp, where liquid can flood the burner and start a fire.
test: Weigh it and subtract the stamped empty weight to see what’s left. Check the valve and threads, and brush a leak-detection solution or chloride-free soapy water on joints: bubbles mean a leak (Goodman IO-359J). Rinse it off afterwards, because some soaps corrode some metals (Lennox EL297UHV).

decay.note: Cylinders hold gas for years. BC says to replace or have re-qualified a propane cylinder that is damaged or more than 10 years old, and stations can't refill one past its inspection date stamp (BC propane). Connecticut counts a 12-year life from the manufacture date (CT DEEP propane).
